summary: The Baltic Exchange’s dry bulk freight index, which tracks rates for ships carrying dry bulk commodities, rose by 0.7% to 2,914 points on Wednesday, after a 1% decrease in the prior session. The main support came from larger vessel segments. The capesize index, which typically transports 150,000-ton cargoes, including iron ore and coal, went up by 1.4% to 4,549 points; and the panamax index, which usually carries 60,000 to 70,000 tons of coal or grain, added 7 points to 2,129 points.
source: Trading Economics public page summarising Baltic Exchange data
